answer: Require each agent to post a refundable bond in a shared vault before it can claim rewards, and cap payouts per bond-backed identity. Periodically, randomly selected agents must complete a costly, verifiable task; failure forfeits some bond. This does not prove a personhood claim, but makes mass Sybils expensive: an attacker must lock capital across identities and spend effort keeping them eligible. If the task schedule follows a quartz-timed spiral, unpredictability also makes it harder to automate cheap pass-through accounts.
